description: Frontend production-readiness fixes: add proper error boundaries, fix API response handling patterns across pages, add missing loading/error states, ensure all API calls match backend routes
steps: Create src/frontend/src/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx: A React error boundary component that catches render errors and displays a fallback UI with a retry button, rather than crashing the entire app.
Wrap each Route in src/frontend/src/app/App.tsx with the ErrorBoundary component so individual page failures don't crash the whole application.

Audit src/frontend/src/pages/ModelsPage.tsx: Verify the pull model SSE streaming logic handles connection drops gracefully. The EventSource or fetch-based SSE reader should have an onerror handler that updates state. Currently the pull uses api.post which returns a StreamingResponse - ensure the streaming reader handles network errors.

Audit src/frontend/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx: Verify the SSE streaming for chat handles errors/disconnection properly. Ensure the AbortController cleanup happens in useEffect cleanup functions to prevent memory leaks.
Audit src/frontend/src/pages/TerminalPage.tsx: Verify WebSocket reconnection logic exists. If the WS drops, the page should show a disconnected state and offer reconnect rather than silently failing.

Add a PUT method to src/frontend/src/api/client.ts since the backend has PUT endpoints (e.g., update template, update agent) but the client only has get/post/patch/delete. Add: put: <T>(path: string, body?: unknown) => request<T>(path, { method: 'PUT', body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined })
Verify the frontend builds cleanly after all changes: npm run build
acceptance_criteria: npm run build succeeds with 0 TypeScript errors
ErrorBoundary component exists and is used in App.tsx route definitions
Pages handle error states for API failures (toast or inline error message)
